block-guide:
CORE/GROUP A container for other blocks: a page section, a card, a row or a stack. Any blocks go inside. The layout attribute decides how the children are placed; the editor's Group, Row, Stack and Grid are this one block with different layouts. MARKUP (checked in the editor)

tagName: "div" (default), "section", "main", "article", "aside", "header", "footer" = the element written in the HTML. Children sit directly inside the element, no inner wrapper. LAYOUT {"type":"constrained"}: children at the theme's content width, centred; a child with align "wide"/"full" breaks out to the wide or full width. Use it for page sections. {"type":"default"} or no layout at all: plain flow, children take the group's full width. {"type":"flex","flexWrap":"nowrap"} = Row; add "orientation":"vertical" for a Stack; justifyContent left|center|right|space-between, verticalAlignment top|center|bottom. {"type":"grid","columnCount":3} = equal columns; or "minimumColumnWidth":"12rem" to wrap. Space between children: style.spacing.blockGap (no inline style in the saved HTML). PITFALLS Never write is-layout-*, wp-container-* or has-global-padding classes: WordPress adds them when it renders the page; they do not belong in saved markup. align "wide"/"full" on a child works only inside a constrained parent (or at the top of the page content); inside a flow group it does nothing. A style variation (themeSettings.styles) may set background and text colour by itself. Colours, padding, border: see the theme settings rules in block-discovery-contract.
